transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-23T16:00Z
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM); Marcus (Calyx Head of Platform), Aisha (Procurement), Diego (Security), Nora (Legal)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align procurement and security on MSA/DPA, confirm KMS/SSO expectations, and agree pilot pricing path. Action: Redwood to send security pack and pilot pricing; Calyx to share traffic profile and sign off on timeline.

Topics covered:
- MSA/DPA redlines and procurement path
- KMS keying (customer-managed) & SSO integration (SAML)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
- Pilot scope, metrics and pricing (committed capacity options)
- Next legal sync and technical benchmark plan

Transcript (partial, auto-transcribed, medium quality; occasional mis-hears):
00:00 Jordan Hayes: okay everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan with Redwood Inference, with me is Priya our solutions eng and Liam from customer success, how's every one?
00:08 Marcus Lee: hey thanks Jordan, Marcus here — excited to get this moving, we got procurement and security on the line to fast-track the onboarding.
00:13 Aisha Rahman: hi I'm Aisha, i'll be shepherding procurement. timeline is tight so want to see MSA and pricing path.
00:18 Diego Morales: Diego, security. quick head's up we need KMS customer-managed keys and SSO (SAML) + SOC2 evidence.
00:25 Jordan Hayes: great — that's exactly what we expected. high-level agenda: MSA/DPA redlines, KMS approach (customer KMS/HSM), SSO, then pilot pricing. We'll record action items.
00:40 Priya Nair: just to add, from an eng standpoint we'll need to run a short benchmark for latency at a 99th percentile target — and verify egress and kv cache behavior.
00:50 Marcus Lee: when you say kv cache, do you mean KV cache? sometimes we get different behaviors in production.
00:55 Priya Nair: yes KV cache - sorry the transcript often says KV cash, but it's KV cache, it's important for prefix reuse.
01:05 Nora Patel: quick procurement/legal Q: does Redwood accept the customer's data residency statement? We're expecting some EU-only controls for a subset of PII.
01:13 Jordan Hayes: short answer: yes we can support EU data residency for the pilot via region pinning or private deployment; we typically document that in the DPA addendum. We'll follow up with the redline.
01:20 Nora Patel: ok. also we may have an addendum around subprocessor list — we'll send that with redlines.
01:28 Diego Morales: on KMS, we need BYOK and HSM support — are there any vendor constraints on key wrap / egress?
01:35 Priya Nair: we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers. There are two patterns: 1) hosted with customer key wrapping where keys are in your KMS and Redwood cannot export them; 2) private deployment where keys remain fully isolated. For hosted we do envelope encryption and can show integration patterns — I'll share a short runbook.
01:55 Diego Morales: cool. and SSO — SAML is must-have, can you support SCIM for provisioning?
02:02 Jordan Hayes: yes SAML + SCIM supported; we map to RBAC roles. we'll include an SSO integration sheet.
02:10 Aisha Rahman: procurement — pricing questions: do you have committed capacity discounts or reserved pools? we need a simple committed model to present to finance.
02:18 Jordan Hayes: absolutely. we have usage-based hosted pricing, and reserved/dedicated pools with monthly/annual commits for unit economics. For pilot we recommend a 3 month reserved pilot with capped egress allowances — we can model three tiers. I'll send a spreadsheet.
02:36 Marcus Lee: and how does fallback work if dedicated capacity saturates? for production we need graceful degradation.
02:42 Priya Nair: routing policies + automatic fallback to compatible model variants — product will route to a lower-cost or lower-latency tier depending on policy. We'll document SLOs and fallback. note: sometimes transcripts show 'fallback to med var' but it's really a variant and model pinning.
03:05 Nora Patel: re MSA redlines: our legal team will ask for indemnity caps and specific data processing flow; do you typically accept our template or is Redwood's template preferred?
03:14 Jordan Hayes: we're flexible; Redwood typically starts with our standard MSA but we've done negotiated redlines. For enterprise terms we can accept certain caps with approval. Let's get your redlines and we'll route internally.
03:25 Aisha Rahman: what's the typical procurement lead time?
03:28 Jordan Hayes: median is 4-6 weeks for enterprise customers once redlines are exchanged; pilot-only minimal internal approvals can be faster — hence our push for pilot.
03:35 Marcus Lee: technical Q from me — we use a mix of short and long context requests; do you support optimized kernels and long-seq behavior?
03:42 Priya Nair: yes, the runtime uses optimized kernels and KV cache management so long-context is supported though performance depends on quantization and sequence length. for the pilot we'll pick a representative model from the catalog and run benchmarks.
04:05 Diego Morales: side question: SOC2, pen tests, and audit logs — we'll need logs for token-level access, traceability.
04:12 Jordan Hayes: we provide audit logs, per-route tracing hooks and token-level billing breakdowns via the Console. SOC2 report and recent pentest summary will be shared.
04:25 Diego Morales: ok also do you support retention controls and data deletion on demand?
04:29 Priya Nair: yes retention windows are configurable; for private or dedicated we can adhere to retention and deletion requests in the DPA.
04:40 Marcus Lee: might need an on-prem package for regulatory reasons, is that on the table?
04:44 Jordan Hayes: yes Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) is an option; we'll scope the work after pilot.
05:00 Aisha Rahman: comical procurement note — finance will want a simple price per 1M tokens and egress lines. any example numbers now?
05:10 Jordan Hayes: I'll avoid precise numbers on call but example tiers will be in the pricing spreadsheet; we'll show hosted vs dedicated per 1M tokens and show committed discount rates.
05:25 Marcus Lee: cool. SLA question — uptime and latency SLOs for dedicated pools?
05:30 Priya Nair: dedicated pools have SLA-backed targets, we usually publish SLOs by model and route. for pilot we can promise best-effort latency and then include latencies in the benchmark readout.
06:00 [~pause while screenshare starts]
07:12 Priya Nair: pulling up the pilot checklist — ideally pilot covers 3 months, expected qps: can you confirm numbers Marcus?
07:22 Marcus Lee: right now we expect 60 qps peak across our agent endpoints and an average 10 qps sustained; gotta check exact distributions.
07:30 Priya Nair: that's helpful. suggests we should size a small dedicated pool with autoscale burst. I'll add cost estimate.
07:40 Diego Morales: are there any data egress costs to internal networks? we are sensitive to cross-region transfer.
07:45 Jordan Hayes: egress costs depend on deployment; we'll explicitly show egress allowances in the pilot sheet.
08:00 Nora Patel: legal follow-up — who will own the DPA negotiation, do you have a contact?
08:05 Jordan Hayes: Nora, I'll be primary for initial redlines and then Redwood legal will take over for final terms.
08:12 Nora Patel: ok please send DPA and subprocessors list.
08:18 Jordan Hayes: will do.
09:00 [Conversation drifts to technical detail — some auto-transcribe artifacts present]
09:10 Priya Nair: small note, when we test model versions we may suggest quantization for cost savings; it'll affect output distribution so we do quality checks.
09:22 Marcus Lee: acceptable as long as we have quality eval test sets and regressions flagged. we have a prompt set we can share.
09:30 Priya Nair: perfect. we'll run evals and post-quality metrics to the Console so you can see regressions.
10:05 Aisha Rahman: procurement wants milestone invoice options for pilot — partial upfront, remainder on acceptance. is that supported?
10:14 Jordan Hayes: yes milestone billing is common. We'll include invoice terms in the pricing spreadsheet and note acceptance criteria.
11:00 Diego Morales: about key rotation — can we rotate keys without downtime?
11:06 Priya Nair: yes, key rotation patterns supported via envelope encryption; we'll note exact steps in runbook.
12:30 Marcus Lee: what's the escalation path if the pilot fails performance thresholds? we want a rollback plan.
12:38 Jordan Hayes: we'll include rollback and fallback policies; Redwood supports model variant fallback and can throttle to maintain availability while we debug.
13:10 [Priya shares a runbook link in chat: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/kms-integration (note: placeholder link)]
13:25 Marcus Lee: thanks — we'll review.
14:00 Nora Patel: one more legal Q — do you accept audit rights for a vendor?
14:07 Jordan Hayes: we accept limited audit rights; we'll provide SOC2 and cooperate on reasonable audits subject to NDAs and scoping.
15:20 Aisha Rahman: procurement timeline — can you commit to providing final pricing sheet by next Wednesday?
15:25 Jordan Hayes: yes we'll send the sheet by 2025-03-26.
15:40 Marcus Lee: technical benchmark week of Apr 7 works, can Priya coordinate?
15:45 Priya Nair: yes I'll reach out after receiving traffic profile.
16:01 [Conversation wraps, recap]
16:05 Jordan Hayes: recap: Jordan sends SOC2/DPA redline pack and pricing spreadsheet by 3/26; Priya sends KMS/SSO runbook and prepares benchmark plan; Marcus shares traffic shape and prompt sets; Nora schedules follow-up legal sync next Tuesday. action items captured in chat.
16:20 Diego Morales: thanks everyone.
16:25 Marcus Lee: thanks, talk soon.
